newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end up, rise tempered by large-lot offer.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end up, rise tempered by large-lot offer.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly higher on Friday after upward momentum ebbed towards the close due to hedge-selling and a large-lot sell order.
"About 700 contracts worth of the September was offered at 126.00, which hampered the key contract's rise," a brokerage house trader said.
Hedge-selling of the September towards the close by traders who bought cash bonds, also tempered its rise, the trader said.
Traders said buying of cash bonds by all types of investors supported JGB futures during the day.
The recent improvement in market sentiment encouraged a variety of investors to buy the newly auctioned 194th 10-year JGB and newly offered government-guaranteed and municipal bonds, they said.

"Every type of investor imaginable was buying. Those who have not yet increased their JGB holdings as much as they would have liked to, gave in and bought, knowing they might have bought on the upside," the brokerage house trader said.
"Investors who had felt that 125.00 would be the high end of the range revised their views after the release of the Bank of Japan's quarterly economic report (on Thursday)," he said.
The September ended at 125.92, up slightly from the previous day's close of 125.78. Turnover was 29,393 contracts.
The September rose to 126.02 during the day, the highest level for any benchmark JGB futures contract since April 25.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.175 percent as of 0644 GMT, down from Thursday's close of 2.205 percent.
The key cash bond yield earlier fell to as low as 2.165 percent, which is its lowest level also since April 25.
The BOJ's report released on Thursday contained a weak economic outlook and has led to a perception that Japanese interest rates will not be raised this year, traders said.
Traders were divided on the near-term outlook for the September.

The September may break above 126.00 relatively easily if the contract manages to stay steady near current levels for a while and prompts traders to buy back their shorts, a trader for a foreign brokerage house said.
JGBs may be capped on the upside, however, as additional buying of cash bonds by investors is unlikely to emerge in the near-term, the first trader said.

"After the buying that has taken place in the last couple of days, I think investor buying of cash bonds has past its peak. I don't think there are too many investors who want to keep buying at current levels," the trader said.
As for next week, traders said they would be watching the preliminary industrial output data for June and forecasts for July and August due on Wednesday.
